note: The pipelines this board ships with: a tree is cut local, and these are the definitions a project's defaultTurnover / defaultInvestigation may name. The live file (pipelines.json, in the panel's state folder) overrides this one per id; docs/pipelines.md is the design. A definition here must pass the same validation as one the reader writes: a stage without an exit, a check outside the closed vocabulary, an unknown {{placeholder}} or a `next` that goes backwards is dropped BY ID and named in the log.

pipelines.title: Local work
pipelines.description: Work in this tree and stop. The LANDING paragraph composed into the prompt decides whether that includes a push and a pull request.

stages.title: Work in this tree
stages.prompt:
Do the work in this tree and stop there. {{desc}}

Commit what you changed in one revertable commit on {{branch}}, then report what you did: the files you touched, the commands you ran and their real results. Where this prompt carries a LANDING paragraph, that paragraph is the only instruction about pushing and opening a pull request: follow it exactly.

pipelines.title: Investigation
pipelines.description: Find out something and write it down, in this tree. Ends by concluding.

stages.title: Probe
stages.prompt:
Find out what is actually being asked: {{desc}}

Read, run and probe in this tree. Record what you ran and what it really returned — the capture, the script, the artefact. Commit the evidence on {{branch}} in one revertable commit. Do not push {{main}} and do not open a pull request.

stages.title: Conclude
stages.prompt: Write the conclusion down in docs/investigation.md: what you found, what you ruled out, and what should happen next. Commit it on {{branch}} and report it in a few lines. Do not push.

pipelines.title: Turnover
pipelines.description: This work is going to land: commit, push the branch and open the pull request, following this host's landing doctrine.

stages.title: Commit
stages.prompt:
Commit everything in this tree on {{branch}} in one revertable commit whose subject names the symptom. {{desc}}

Do not push yet.

stages.title: Push the branch
stages.prompt: Push the branch, never {{main}}: git push -u origin {{branch}}. If the write is refused, report the refusal and stop — the panel's permission box is the only thing that can grant it.

stages.title: Open the pull request
stages.prompt: Open ONE pull request from {{branch}} into {{main}}, following this project's landing doctrine — the host is {{host}}, and the doctrine names the title, the reviewers and the description sections. Report the PR URL. Leave it open: this definition does not merge.

pipelines.title: GitHub investigation
pipelines.description: Find out something on a GitHub project, write it down, and stop there — the work may chain into a turnover if it concludes the change has to land.

stages.title: Probe
stages.prompt:
Find out what is actually being asked: {{desc}}

Read, run and probe in this tree. Record what you ran and what it really returned — the capture, the script, the artefact. Commit the evidence on {{branch}} in one revertable commit. Do not push yet.

stages.title: Conclude
stages.prompt: Write the conclusion down in docs/investigation.md: what you found, what you ruled out, and what should happen next. Commit it on {{branch}} and report it in a few lines. This tree stays local until the reader turns the conclusion into a turnover.

pipelines.title: SEFL investigation
pipelines.description: Find out something on a SEFL Bitbucket project, write it down, and stop there — the work may chain into the review loop if it concludes the change has to land.

stages.title: Probe
stages.prompt:
Find out what is actually being asked: {{desc}}

Read, run and probe in this tree — {{tree}} on {{branch}}, from the {{host}} repository this project maps to. Record what you ran and what it really returned. Commit the evidence on {{branch}} in one revertable commit. Do not push yet.

stages.title: Conclude
stages.prompt: Write the conclusion down in docs/investigation.md: what you found, what you ruled out, and what should happen next. Commit it on {{branch}} and report it in a few lines. This tree stays local until the reader turns the conclusion into a turnover.

pipelines.title: GitHub force merge
pipelines.description: The turnover pipeline for a GitHub project whose reader named it: commit, version, push, open the PR, merge with --admin (the ruleset's bypass) and confirm main moved.

stages.title: Commit
stages.prompt: Commit everything in this tree on {{branch}}, one revertable commit whose subject names the symptom. {{desc}}

stages.title: Version
stages.prompt: Run `node tools/version.mjs suggest`, judge the level against what changed, apply it in the same commit and put the reason in the commit body. The stage is done when `node tools/version.mjs check` exits 0.

stages.title: Push the branch
stages.prompt: Push the branch, never {{main}}: git push -u origin {{branch}}. If the push is refused, report the refusal and stop — the permission box is the only thing that grants a write.

stages.title: Open the pull request
stages.prompt:
Open ONE pull request from {{branch}} into {{main}} and read it back before reporting it:

  gh pr create --fill

When this branch carries a version bump, --fill drops the reason the bump gave, so pass --title and --body-file instead and put the level and its reason into the body. Then run `gh pr view <n> --json state,headRefOid,baseRefName` and confirm headRefOid is the commit you just pushed. Report the PR URL.

stages.title: Merge
stages.prompt:
Merge the pull request for {{branch}}: gh pr merge --rebase --admin.

--admin is the ruleset's bypass, not a preference: the repository's ruleset, "Owner only" (id 25783530, docs/pushing-to-a-remote.md gate 8), refuses an update to the default branch except through a bypass. --rebase keeps {{main}} linear, which the ruleset requires; --merge would be refused.

If the merge fails because this account has no bypass, say exactly that and report instead of retrying.

stages.title: Confirm main moved
stages.prompt: Run `git fetch origin {{main}}` and confirm the merge is on it: the commit you merged is reachable from origin/{{main}}. Report the sha.

pipelines.title: SEFL review loop
pipelines.description: Cut a correctly named turnover branch, open a PR for code_review_java, answer what arrives, merge when approved.

stages.title: Name the branch
stages.prompt: Rename this tree's branch to YYYYMMDD_HHMM_<TICKET>_<desc> and nothing else: the cut's own local time, the ticket id the work names ({{ticket}}), and <desc> as lowercase words joined by underscores. Example: 20261102_1431_ABC-1234_fix_login_redirect. Then report the new name.

stages.title: Push the branch
stages.prompt: Push the branch, never {{main}}: git push origin {{branch}}. If the push is refused, report the refusal and stop — the panel's permission box is the only thing that grants a write.

stages.title: Open the pull request
stages.prompt:
Open ONE pull request from {{branch}} into {{main}} on the project's {{host}}, following the landing doctrine exactly:

- title: "Java Code Review for <repo> <branch>"
- reviewers: the GROUP code_review_java and nothing else — no individuals, no DAL group on a non-DAL change
- description, four sections, every one present: ## Jira Ticket, ## Description, ## Test Procedures, ## Technical Specifications

POST it to the host's pull-request endpoint with the landing doctrine's REST path and bearer token, fromRef refs/heads/{{branch}}, toRef refs/heads/{{main}}. Read the PR back: reviewers must be exactly [code_review_java], and fromRef.latestCommit must be the head you pushed. Report the PR id and URL.

stages.title: Wait for the reviewer
stages.prompt: Read the PR's activities once (the landing doctrine names the endpoint). Report what arrived, then END the turn: say plainly that nothing has arrived if nothing has. Do not sleep, do not poll in a loop, and do not merge — the panel re-checks on its own clock and wakes this thread when there is something to answer.

stages.title: Answer the review
stages.prompt: For each new comment on the PR for {{branch}}: make the smallest change that answers it, commit on {{branch}}, push, and reply on that comment naming the commit. Then report what you answered. An approval at an older commit is not an approval of the head — after any push the head needs re-approval.

stages.title: Wait for the approval at the head
stages.prompt: Nothing to say: wait for the head to be reviewed. The stage ends when an approval exists whose lastReviewedCommit equals the PR's current head ({{sha}}). Report the reviewer and the commit they approved.

stages.title: Merge
stages.prompt: Merge the PR for {{branch}} with its current version: POST the host's merge endpoint (the landing doctrine names it) with the PR id and ?version=<the PR's current version>. Then confirm {{main}} moved. Never push {{main}} directly and never decline or close the PR.
